records.evidence: AXS-02 is an oral osteoclast inhibitor; a mechanistic observation does not establish analgesic efficacy.
IDMC reviewed safety in CREATE-1 and reported acceptable tolerability; no trial-specific event counts were disclosed in this interim statement.

IDMC reviewed safety in COAST-1 and reported acceptable tolerability; no trial-specific event counts were disclosed in this interim statement.

Registry status is UNKNOWN (last updated 2018-03-23), whereas issuer disclosed IDMC recommendation to stop CREATE-1 for futility. Do not present this as an active trial. A reconciled final registry status is unresolved.
CREATE-1 interim analysis (81 participants): IDMC recommended stopping for futility. This is an interim futility outcome, not a fabricated final primary p-value.
Serum CTx reduction versus placebo p<0.0001 was pharmacologic activity, not the pain primary endpoint.
COAST-1 interim sample-size/safety review included 77 subjects and recommended continuation; this is not proof of primary-endpoint success.
STRIDE-1 Week-6 MADRS primary endpoint did not meet significance: reductions 11.6 with AXS-05 versus 9.4 with bupropion, p=0.117. Later MDD approval does not change this result.
Active-comparator primary comparison at Week6 was nonsignificant; earlier and averaged secondary comparisons do not replace it.
FOCUS randomized 516 adults. At Week6, 150mg AISRS reduction was 17.7 versus 14.3 with placebo, p=0.039. These figures do not establish a positive 300mg primary comparison.
150mg clinical response (AISRS improvement at least30%) was 53.5% versus41.3% with placebo; CGI-S secondary p=0.017. Clinical importance requires separate evaluation.

PARADIGM did not achieve statistical significance on MADRS in the overall randomized population. Any EDS subgroup findings remain separate and do not turn the overall trial into a primary-endpoint success.
SYMPHONY weekly cataplexy primary at Week5: reductions83% with AXS-12 versus66% with placebo, p=0.018.
ENCORE:68 enrolled in open-label treatment;42 entered randomized withdrawal. Cataplexy withdrawal comparison favored continued AXS-12, p=0.017. Do not use68 as randomized efficacy denominator.
Among68 ENCORE participants, nausea and tachycardia each occurred in5.9%; AE discontinuations17.6%.
ENCORE AE discontinuations were17.6% over the reported long-term experience; the blinded period separately had0 AXS-12 and1 placebo AE discontinuation.

EMERGE issuer reports improved mTOQ-4 (5.2 versus2.8, p<0.001) after switching96 patients from prior oral CGRP treatment. Open-label within-person comparison is not a randomized active-control superiority result.

Issuer labels mTOQ-4 as primary, but current registry lists headache pain relief and most-bothersome-symptom percentages. Reconcile protocol/registry history before an unqualified primary-endpoint adjudication.
